Player's manual · version 0.8.0

3D Fighter

One-on-one fights in 3D, with a camera that moves in on the action. Seven fighters, eight stages, and online play with spectators.

01Getting started

Download the build for your computer from the releases page, unpack it, and run it. There's no installer.

SystemDownloadHow to start
Windows 10/11 (64-bit)3DFighter-v0.8.0-windows.zipUnzip and run 3DFighter.exe. If SmartScreen warns you (indie games aren't code-signed), click More info → Run anyway.
macOS 11+ (Apple Silicon and Intel)3DFighter-v0.8.0-macos.zipUnzip and open 3DFighter.app. It's signed and notarized by Apple. Allow local network access if you want to play on your network.
Linux (x86_64, also Steam Deck)3DFighter-v0.8.0-linux.tar.gztar xzf the archive and run 3DFighter/3DFighter.x86_64.

You need a graphics card with Vulkan support. The game runs at 60 frames a second on integrated graphics at 720p. A gamepad is optional; two can be connected for local two-player matches.

Choosing fighters and stages

03Controls

Directions are always relative to the screen. "Forward" means toward your opponent, so it flips when you switch sides. The game handles that for you.

ActionPlayer 1 keyboardPlayer 2 keyboardGamepad
Move / jump / crouchW A S DArrow keysD-pad or left stick
LP Light PunchUNum 4 or [X
HP Heavy PunchINum 5 or ]Y
LK Light KickJNum 1 or ;A
HK Heavy KickKNum 2 or 'B
SS SidestepLNum 6 or /RB
PauseEscStart

Gamepad 1 is Player 1 and gamepad 2 is Player 2. With a single pad you can give it to Player 2 in Options. Every button can be changed in Options → Controls. Gamepad labels follow the Xbox layout.

04Fighting basics

Matches are best of three rounds. Each round lasts 99 seconds. Knock your opponent out, or have more health left (as a share of your maximum) when time runs out.

Moving

  • Walk: hold forward or back.
  • Dash and backdash: tap forward twice, or back twice.
  • Jump: up, up-forward or up-back. You can attack once in the air.
  • Crouch: hold down. High attacks pass over a crouching fighter.
  • Sidestep: SS steps into the screen; hold down while pressing it to step toward the camera. A sidestep slips past straight attacks and fireballs, and the fight turns to follow you.

Attacking

Four buttons: LP HP LK HK. Light attacks are fast and safe; heavy ones hit harder but leave you open if they miss. Each button does something different when you hold a direction:

  • Standing: the button alone.
  • Crouching: hold down. ↓HP is an uppercut that launches the opponent into the air, and ↓HK sweeps them off their feet.
  • Forward: hold forward for each fighter's two signature moves (see The fighters).
  • In the air: any button during a jump. Jump attacks hit overhead.
  • Throw: LP + LK together, up close. Throws can't be blocked.

Blocking

Hold back (away from your opponent) to block. There is no block button. Attacks come at four heights:

Attack heightBlock it byExamples
HighHolding back, or just crouching (it whiffs)Jab, straight, roundhouse
MidHolding back or down-backMid kick, crouching jab, uppercut
LowHolding down-back onlyLow kick, sweep, Gale Slide, Earthquake
OverheadHolding back while standing onlyEvery jump attack, Axe Kick, Overhead Smash
ThrowCan't be blocked: press LP+LK just as you're grabbed to break itThrows. Command grabs can't be broken at all.

If an attack is already coming at you when you hold back, you block in place instead of walking away.

05The fight screen

  1. Health. Player 1 on the left, Player 2 on the right.
  2. Round timer. Turns red in the last 10 seconds.
  3. Name and round wins. A circle lights up for each round won; two wins takes the match.
  4. Damage trail. Recent damage shows in red before the bar drains.
  5. Super meter. Fills as you hit and get hit. When it's full and glowing gold, you can use your super.

The action camera

The camera starts side-on. As a fight heats up (combos, juggles, big hits), it swings around behind the attacker's shoulder and moves in on the fighter taking the hits, then eases back when things calm down. Controls never change with the camera. If you prefer a fixed view, set Action Camera to Subtle or Off in Options.

Before the first round of a match, each fighter gets a short intro: a close-up, their own pose and a line, with special lines when rivals meet. Press any attack button to skip it, or turn intros off in Options.

Fight announcements appear in the middle of the screen: ROUND 1, FIGHT!, K.O., TIME, PERFECT (won without losing any health), COUNTER and combo counts.

The pause menu

06Specials, supers and combos

Reading move notation

Special moves are entered with a motion and a button. The manual, the move list and character select write motions as arrows, shown for a fighter facing right. Numbers follow a numeric keypad, with 5 as neutral:

7↖8↑9↗ 4←56→ 1↙2↓3↘
MotionArrowsName
236↓↘→Quarter circle forward
214↓↙←Quarter circle back
623→↓↘Dragon punch
63214→↘↓↙←Half circle back
236236↓↘→↓↘→Double quarter circle: supers

P means either punch and K either kick. Roll through the directions smoothly and press the button at the end. You don't need to be exact about timing, just quick. When you're on the right side of the screen, the motions mirror.

Supers

When your super meter is full, enter your fighter's super motion (↓↘→↓↘→ plus a punch or kick). The fight freezes for a moment while the fighter's face sweeps across the screen, then the super plays out: a long flurry of hits that ends in a finisher. It uses the whole meter. The meter fills when you land attacks, when your attacks are blocked, and when you get hit, and it carries over between rounds.

Combos

  • Chains. Some normals flow into others when they hit or are blocked. For example, Jab → Jab → Straight.
  • Cancels. A normal attack that connects can be cancelled into a special move, and a special into your super.
  • Juggles. Launchers (the uppercut, rising specials, Valka's knee) knock the opponent into the air, where you can keep hitting them. After three hits in the air they can't be hit again until they land.
  • Counter hits. Hit someone while they're starting an attack and you do 25% more damage, and they're stunned longer. "COUNTER" appears on screen.
  • Damage scaling. Each hit in a combo does 10% less than the last, down to 30%. Big damage comes from strong starters, not endless combos.
  • Corners. When your opponent is pinned at the edge, you get pushed back instead of them, unless the hit splats them.
  • Wall splats. Drive a stunned opponent into the edge of the stage with a heavy hit (a roundhouse, a charge, a big palm strike) and they splat against it: stuck there for a moment and open to a follow-up, before they crumple to the floor. The splat costs them a little health, and it only happens once per combo. "WALL SPLAT" appears on screen. On the Boxing Ring they bounce off the ropes instead, straight back toward you and high enough to hit again ("ROPE BOUNCE").

Reversal: for a moment after Still Water starts, any high, mid or overhead attack that touches her is caught (jump-ins too), and she throws the attacker. The throw can't be blocked or broken. Lows, throws and fireballs go straight through, and a stance that catches nothing leaves her wide open, so use it when you know an attack is coming. Against Lian, sweep, throw, or wait it out.

Picking the same fighter as your opponent gives Player 2 an alternate look, so you can tell the two apart.

08Stages

Each stage has its own music. Every arena is the same length; the Express is narrower, so there's less room to sidestep on the train roof. The Kowloon Courtyard changes as the match goes on: it starts at dawn and the sun climbs with every round.

09Vs CPU, Arcade and Versus

Vs CPU

Pick your fighter, your opponent and a stage. The CPU's difficulty (Easy, Normal or Hard) is set in Options. Each fighter has a personality as the CPU: Kenji keeps his distance and throws fireballs, Rhea rushes you, Brutus waits to punish, Valka hunts for grabs, Jin plays at the edge of his reach, Mira powers up whenever you give her room, and Lian waits for you to swing, then turns it into a throw.

Arcade

Choose a fighter and take on every other fighter in turn, each on a different stage picked at random for the run (no stage twice). The opponents get tougher as you go. The final boss is your own shadow, in the Dojo: a darker copy of your fighter on Hard, who starts every round with a full super meter.

  • Score: 10 points per point of damage dealt. Each round won adds a time bonus (100 per second left), a life bonus (up to 5,000) and 10,000 for a perfect round. Each stage cleared adds 10,000 × the stage number.
  • Losing: choose Continue to retry the stage from the score you started it with, or Give Up.
  • Records: your best run with each fighter is saved and shown under Best Scores. Clear the boss to see the credits.

Versus (2 Players)

Two players on one computer, with a keyboard each side or two gamepads (see Controls). Player 1 picks first, then Player 2, each with their own controls: up and down to choose, Light Punch to confirm, Heavy Punch to go back.

10Training

Pick your fighter and a dummy, then practice with no timer and no knockouts. Health refills after each combo, and your super meter is always full.

Frame data

The game runs at 60 frames a second, and every move is measured in frames:

  • Startup: frames before the move can hit. Lower is faster.
  • Active: frames during which it can hit.
  • Recovery: frames after, before you can act again.
  • On hit / on block: who recovers first, measured as it happens. +5 means you can act 5 frames before your opponent; a negative number means they act first, and a big negative number means you can be punished. KD means the move knocked them down.

The training menu

SettingChoices
DummyStand, Crouch, Jump, CPU (fights back), or Playback (repeats a recording)
GuardNone, Block All, Block After First Hit, or Random
Health Refill, Infinite MeterOn or off
Frame Data, Input History, HitboxesShow or hide each panel; Hitboxes draws the attack and body areas
Combo TrialOff (free training), or one of your fighter's combo trials; a tick marks the ones you've done

Combo trials

Every fighter has five or six combo trials, from a simple chain to a corner combo and their super. Choose one under Combo Trial in the training menu (or press Page Down in training to start the first). The panel on the right lists the moves to land, in order, in one combo; if you drop the combo or use a different move, the trial starts over. Clear it and "SUCCESS!" appears, then the next trial starts. Your progress is saved.

  • F8 (or R3) shows you the trial: your fighter plays it once. Press F8 again to stop.
  • Page Up / Page Down go to the previous or next trial, and Backspace starts the current one over.
  • Trials set up the dummy for you: standing, not blocking, and at the edge of the stage for a corner trial. Your meter is only full for a trial that ends in your super, so a sloppy motion can't come out as the super instead of the special.

Recording the dummy

Press F6 to take control of the dummy and record up to 10 seconds of its moves, then F6 again to stop. The dummy then repeats the recording over and over, which is useful for practicing against a specific attack or pressure. F7 pauses and resumes playback. Backspace (or L3) puts both fighters back at their starting positions.

11Online play

Choose Online in the main menu. Both players need the same version of the game.

Way to playWhen to use itHow
Internet LobbyOver the internet: the easy waySee The Internet Lobby. No router setup.
Games on your networkSame home or office networkOne player chooses Host Game; the other sees it in the list and picks it.
Join by addressOver the internet, without the lobbyThe host forwards UDP port 7777 on their router and shares their public IP address; the other player types it and chooses Join.

The host always gets asked to accept a player before they're let in. Then both pick fighters, the host picks the stage, and you fight.

How online matches feel

The game uses rollback netcode. It predicts your opponent's input so your own moves respond instantly, and if the prediction was wrong it corrects the fight a moment later. On a good connection you won't notice; on a poor one you might see the occasional small jump. The bar at the bottom of the screen shows the connection quality, your ping, how many frames were corrected (rollback) and the input delay.

Security

Online connections are encrypted. Both players see the same 6-digit security code in character select and in the leave prompt. If the codes match, nobody is listening in. If they differ, leave the match.

An online match can't be paused. Esc asks whether you want to leave. After a match choose Rematch (both players have to ask), Character Select, or Leave.

12The Internet Lobby

The lobby server introduces players to each other, so nobody has to change router settings. Choose Online → Internet Lobby.

  1. Connect. Check your name, then press Connect. The server address is already filled in. Next to ROOMS you can see how many players are online, how many are in a match and how many are watching.
  2. Join a room from the list with Join, or type a friend's 6-letter room code and press Join. If a room has a password, type it in the Password box first.
  3. Or open your own room with Open a Room:
    • Listed: show the room in everyone's list. Untick it for a private room that only people with the code can find.
    • Spectators: let other people watch your matches.
    • Password (optional): only people who know it can join or watch.

Once you're connected, both players go to character select and everything works as in any online match. The status line shows whether you're connected directly or through the server's relay.

Direct or relay

The game first tries to connect the two players directly, which gives the lowest ping. If that doesn't work within about three seconds (some home routers and mobile networks block it), the match goes through the server's relay instead. That always works, but it adds the trip to the server and back.

Hide my IP address

Tick Hide my IP address before connecting to always play through the relay. Your opponent then never learns your IP address. It can add some ping, depending on how far you both are from the server. Either way, the match is encrypted end to end: the server passes the data along without being able to read it.

13Watching matches

Press Watch on a room in the lobby, or type its code and press Watch. Watching works in any room that allows spectators.

  • A short delay. You watch about 3 seconds behind the players, so nobody can coach a player live.
  • Joining late is fine. If the match has been going for a while, the game fast-forwards to the present in a few seconds.
  • It's the real match. Your game replays the players' inputs and checks the result against the host's own game as it goes. If the two ever disagreed (a different game version, say), the replay would stop with "OUT OF SYNC" rather than show you a different fight.
  • Reactions. Press 1 to 6 to send CLAP, FIRE, WOW, HAHA, GG or OUCH. Everyone in the room sees them.
  • Rematches. You stay in the room between matches; the next match loads when it starts. Esc asks whether you want to stop watching.

14Options

OptionWhat it does
Music, Effects and Announcer volumeEach one separately.
Ambience volumeEach stage's background sound (rain, waves, street noise) and the crowd, which cheers louder as the action heats up and reacts to big hits, counters, combos, supers and knockouts. Slide it all the way down to turn it off.
Action CameraFull, Subtle (half the movement) or Off (always side-on).
CPU DifficultyEasy, Normal or Hard for Vs CPU. Arcade starts one step easier and gets harder as you climb.
Fight IntrosEach fighter's pose and line before the first round of an offline match. Any attack button skips one; switch them off here.
DisplayWindowed, Borderless Fullscreen or Exclusive Fullscreen. Fullscreen always uses your desktop resolution.
Window SizeThe window's size when Windowed (sizes bigger than your screen are greyed out).
ResolutionHow many lines the fight is drawn at, scaled up to the screen (720p to 1440p, or Native). Menus and text stay sharp. The default, 1080p, doubles the frame rate on high-resolution laptop screens compared with Native.
GraphicsHigh shows every effect. Medium renders at 85% of the chosen resolution with lighter anti-aliasing and fewer particles. Low renders at 75% and turns off glow, haze, rain and other particles, and reflections: up to about 1.8× the frame rate on laptops and integrated graphics.
Gamepad 1 is Player 2Gives the first gamepad to Player 2, handy with a single pad in Versus.
Controls…Select an action, then press the new key or button. If it's already used, the two actions swap. Esc or Start cancels. Reset to Defaults restores the original layout. Movement on a gamepad always uses the D-pad and left stick.

15Troubleshooting

My special moves don't come out

Do the motion a little faster and press the button right at the end. Check the direction: motions are written for a fighter facing right, so mirror them when you're on the right side. Training's input history shows exactly what you entered.

I can't see my friend's game on our network

Make sure you're both on the same network: guest Wi-Fi and VPNs often hide games from each other. Allow the game through your firewall if asked. On a Mac, allow local network access. Or just use the Internet Lobby.

The lobby says it can't connect to the server

Check your internet connection. If the server is being updated, try again in a few minutes. If you once typed your own server address, the lobby keeps using it: type the official address instead and connect once, and from then on the lobby follows the official server again. The current official address is listed in online/servers.json.

"Different game version" or "That room runs a different version of the game"

Both players, and spectators, need the same version of the game. Download the latest from the releases page. The lobby tells you when a newer version is out.

The online match feels laggy

Check the bar at the bottom: a ping under 100 ms plays well. Use a wired connection if you can, and close downloads and streams. If you ticked Hide my IP address, untick it to allow a direct connection, which is usually faster.

The camera moves too much

Set Action Camera to Subtle or Off in Options.
